title: Compute an edit distance with asymmetric operation costs
levels: Meets every requirement in the brief
Misses at least one requirement in the brief

cases.rationale: It computes the standard Levenshtein distance with every operation costing 1, so edit_distance("abc", "ab") returns 1 and edit_distance("kitten", "sitting") returns 3 instead of 2 and 5.
A full dynamic-programming table charges deletions 2, insertions 1 and replacements 2 in the right directions and compares characters exactly.
It casefolds both strings first, so edit_distance("Apple", "apple") returns 0 instead of 2, while the pasted pytest log claims test_case_matters_apple passed.
A single in-place row with a carried diagonal applies the brief's three costs in the right directions and compares characters exactly.
